Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner reads /proc/<pid>/environ (Claude Code prompt-injection cred-theft)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Self-hosted Actions runner egress to non-allowlisted host during claude-code-action execution
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner reads /proc/<pid>/environ (Claude Code prompt-injection cred-theft) Installation High
Hunts the exact technique RyotaK used to weaponise the Claude Code GitHub Action: a prompt-injected issue body coaxes Claude into shelling out and dumping /proc/self/environ to harvest ANTHROPIC_API_KEY plus ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN / URL. Detection fires when any process under a self-hosted Actions runner ancestry reads /proc/*/environ. Not relevant to GitHub-hosted runners (no telemetry), only self-hosted Linux runner fleets. Rationale: Anchored on the exact exfil mechanic RyotaK described (Claude bypassing the naive /proc/self/environ guard) and bound to a self-hosted runner ancestry (Runner.Worker / _work/_actions / claude-code-action). v1.0.94 patches env-var scrubbing for child processes, so any post-patch hit on this rule on a self-hosted runner is highly indicative of either an unpatched action OR a bypass; pre-patch it is the primary IOC. Cross-checked against GMO Flatt Security writeup and Cybersecurity News article. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/claude-codes-github-actions-vulnerability/ • https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/security.md
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1059.004 T1078.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ProcessCommandLine has "/environ"
| where FileName in~ ("cat","head","xxd","od","strings","tr","awk","grep","sed","tail","dd","sh","bash","python","python3","node")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker","_work/_actions","_work/_temp","claude-code-action","anthropics/claude-code")
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/actions-runner/","/runner/_work/","_actions/anthropics")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "ProcessCreated"
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has "/proc/" and ActingProcessCommandLine has "/environ"
| where ActingProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(/|^)(cat|head|xxd|od|strings|tr|awk|grep|sed|tail|dd|sh|bash|python3?|node)$"
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("Runner.Worker","_work/_actions","_work/_temp","claude-code-action","anthropics/claude-code")
    or ParentProcessName has_any ("Runner.Worker","Runner.Listener")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: GitHub Actions Self-Hosted Runner Reads /proc/self/environ (Claude Code Injection)
id: 9c3a5e1f-2b88-4f51-8df1-9c12b3d2a17e
description: Detects a Linux process under a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner ancestry that reads /proc/<pid>/environ - the technique used in RyotaK's claude-code-action prompt-injection chain to steal ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN credentials from the workflow env.
references:
  - https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/claude-code-github-action-flaw-let-one.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1552.001
  - attack.t1059.004
  - attack.credential_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: linux
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '/cat'
      - '/head'
      - '/xxd'
      - '/od'
      - '/strings'
      - '/tr'
      - '/awk'
      - '/grep'
      - '/sed'
      - '/tail'
      - '/dd'
      - '/bash'
      - '/sh'
      - '/python'
      - '/python3'
      - '/node'
  selection_target:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - '/proc/'
      - '/environ'
  selection_runner_ctx:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'Runner.Worker'
      - '_work/_actions'
      - '_work/_temp'
      - 'claude-code-action'
      - 'anthropics/claude-code'
  condition: selection_image and selection_target and selection_runner_ctx
falsepositives:
  - Developer or SRE manually debugging a workflow env
  - Process-introspection tooling (osquery, psutil-based monitoring) that legitimately inspects /proc
level: high
source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE (@process.command_line:(*"/proc/self/environ"* OR *"/environ"*)) (@process.executable.path:(*/cat OR */head OR */xxd OR */od OR */strings OR */tr OR */awk OR */grep OR */sed OR */tail OR */bash OR */sh OR */python OR */python3 OR */node) OR @process.name:(cat OR head OR xxd OR od OR strings OR bash OR sh OR python OR python3 OR node)) (@process.parent_process.command_line:(*"Runner.Worker"* OR *"_work/_actions"* OR *"claude-code-action"* OR *"anthropics/claude-code"*) OR @process.executable.path:*"/actions-runner/"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| event_platform=Lin
| CommandLine=/\/proc\/(self|[0-9]+)\/environ/i
| ImageFileName=/\/(cat|head|xxd|od|strings|tr|awk|grep|sed|tail|dd|bash|sh|python3?|node)$/i
| ParentCommandLine=/(Runner\.Worker|_work\/_actions|_work\/_temp|claude-code-action|anthropics\/claude-code|actions-runner)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count(as=executions))
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cat","head","xxd","od","strings","tr","awk","grep","sed","tail","python","python3","node","bash","sh","dd")) AND Processes.process="*/proc/*environ*" by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where match(parent_process, "(?i)Runner\.Worker|_work/_actions|_work/_temp|claude-code-action|anthropics/claude-code")
   OR match(parent_process_path, "(?i)actions-runner|/runner/_work")
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("cat","head","xxd","od","strings","tr","awk","grep","sed","tail","python","python3","node","bash","sh","dd")) AND Processes.process="*/proc/*environ*" by host Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.parent_process_path
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| where match(parent_process, "(?i)Runner\.Worker|_work/_actions|_work/_temp|claude-code-action|anthropics/claude-code")
   OR match(parent_process_path, "(?i)actions-runner|/runner/_work")
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] Self-hosted Actions runner egress to non-allowlisted host during claude-code-action execution Command & Control Medium
Catches the exfiltration leg of the chain: prompt-injected Claude making outbound HTTP(S) from the runner to attacker infrastructure (article notes Claude can be coaxed to embed stolen secrets in URL path args via `gh`, `curl`, `wget` or node `fetch`). Allowlists the only destinations a legitimate claude-code-action job should hit (GitHub APIs, Anthropic, github-hosted release/object stores, GitHub App auth) — anything else from a Claude-Code-context process is a candidate for token exfil. Rationale: Allowlist is derived directly from the action's documented integrations (GitHub APIs for repo ops, Anthropic for the LLM, package mirrors for setup-* actions). The v1.0.94 fix that 'blocks exfiltration-capable URL patterns' confirms outbound URL-arg abuse was the real exfil channel, so any unexpected destination from a runner-context node/python/curl/wget/gh process is the signal. Cross-checked against the GMO Flatt Security writeup (specifically the gh-CLI weaponisation section) and the v1.0.94 security.md. Cross-checked against: • https://flatt.tech/research/posts/poisoning-claude-code-one-github-issue-to-break-the-supply-chain/ • https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action/blob/main/docs/security.md • https://cyberpress.org/claude-code-github-actions-flaw/
ATT&CKT1567 T1041 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
let RunnerCtx = dynamic(["/actions-runner/","/_work/_actions/","claude-code-action","anthropics/claude-code","Runner.Worker"]);
let Allowlist = dynamic([".github.com",".githubusercontent.com",".githubapp.com",".anthropic.com","claude.ai",".npmjs.org",".pypi.org",".archive.ubuntu.com",".deb.debian.org",".docker.io",".microsoft.com",".azure.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","python","python3","curl","wget","gh")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (RunnerCtx) or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (RunnerCtx)
| extend Host = tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host)
| where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| where not(Host has_any (Allowlist))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, Host, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
let RunnerCtx = dynamic(["/actions-runner/","/_work/_actions/","claude-code-action","anthropics/claude-code","Runner.Worker"]);
let Allowlist = dynamic([".github.com",".githubusercontent.com",".githubapp.com",".anthropic.com","claude.ai",".npmjs.org",".pypi.org",".archive.ubuntu.com",".deb.debian.org",".docker.io",".microsoft.com",".azure.com"]);
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where SrcUsername contains "runner" or SrcHostname has_any ("runner","actions")
| where isnotempty(Url)
| extend Host = tostring(parse_url(Url).Host)
| where not(Host has_any (Allowlist))
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcUsername, DstHostname, Url, Host, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |

    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
High

China-Linked TA4922 Expands Phishing Attacks to U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa

The Hacker News
2026-06-04 14 use cases 7 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

A new China-linked cybercrime group known as TA4922 has expanded its targeting focus to target European organizations in the U.K., Germany, Italy, and South Africa. These efforts have been complemented by a "rapid operational tempo" and a continually evolving malware arsenal comprising known families like ValleyRAT (aka Winos 4.0) and Atlas RAT (aka AtlasCross RAT), as well as previously

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender · Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TA4922 Atlas RAT / RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader Known SHA256 Execution · [LLM] RomulusLoader: AnyDesk or SyncFuture written/spawned from non-installer parent · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TA4922 Known C2 IPs and Domains (Proofpoint Jun-2026) · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] SilentRunLoader: Python process touching Chrome Login Data / Cookies / Local State · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] TA4922 Known C2 IPs and Domains (Proofpoint Jun-2026) Command & Control High
Hunts host- and network-layer touches of the six TA4922 C2 IPs and three domains tied to Atlas RAT / RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader staging from the Proofpoint write-up. Article-specific because the IOC set is unique to this campaign cluster. Rationale: Six C2 IPs + three domains are explicitly enumerated in the Proofpoint-derived IOC bundle and are unique to the TA4922 cluster. Direct IOC match — no behavioural heuristic needed.

[LLM] TA4922 Atlas RAT / RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader Known SHA256 Execution Installation High
Hunts execution or file-drop of the eight TA4922 payload hashes Proofpoint disclosed. Article-specific because the hash set ties directly to the Atlas RAT / RomulusLoader / SilentRunLoader builds used in the March-April 2026 UK/Germany/Italy/SA campaigns. Rationale: Eight SHA256s are explicitly tied to Atlas RAT, RomulusLoader and SilentRunLoader payloads in the article-supplied IOC bundle. Hash match is the highest-fidelity pivot available.

[LLM] SilentRunLoader: Python process touching Chrome Login Data / Cookies / Local State Actions on Objectives High
Hunts the SilentRunLoader pattern from the article — a Python-based loader (or its dropped EXE) reading Chrome credential / cookie / DPAPI master-key files. Article explicitly calls out Chrome credential, cookie and browsing-history harvest by a 'vibe-coded Python loader' delivered via UK tax-themed lures. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out a Python-based SilentRunLoader dropping an EXE to harvest Chrome credentials, cookies and browsing data. Pivot on python.exe + Chrome credential-vault paths is precisely the documented behaviour.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
let ChromeArtifacts = dynamic([
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cookies",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Network\Cookies",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\History",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Web Data",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Local State"
]);
let StagingPaths = dynamic([@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FolderPath has_any (ChromeArtifacts) or FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","Local State","Web Data")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe","py.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (StagingPaths)
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","chromedriver.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
let ChromeArtifacts = dynamic([
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cookies",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Network\Cookies",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\History",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Web Data",
  @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Local State"
]);
let StagingPaths = dynamic([@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\", @"\Downloads\", @"\ProgramData\"]);
let PythonBins = dynamic(["python.exe","pythonw.exe","py.exe"]);
let BrowserBins = dynamic(["chrome.exe","chromedriver.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (ChromeArtifacts) or TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","Local State","Web Data")
| extend ActingBin = tolower(ActingProcessName)
| where (ActingBin in (PythonBins))
   or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (StagingPaths))
| where not (ActingBin in (BrowserBins))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] RomulusLoader: AnyDesk or SyncFuture written/spawned from non-installer parent Installation Medium
Hunts the RomulusLoader hand-off from the Mid-April 2026 campaign — the loader deploys AnyDesk and SyncFuture via DLL side-loading rather than the vendor installer. Article-specific: legitimate AnyDesk/SyncFuture installs come from msiexec / vendor setup; spawning from a script-host, archive extractor or temp-path parent is the documented TA4922 pattern. Rationale: Article states the Mid-April 2026 campaign uses RomulusLoader to deploy AnyDesk and SyncFuture via DLL side-loading. Legitimate installs originate from msiexec / vendor setup binary in Program Files; everything else against these two specific binaries is high-signal because SyncFuture is uncommon enterprise software.
ATT&CKT1219 T1574.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let LegitInstallers = dynamic(["msiexec.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe","explorer.exe","services.exe","wusa.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","anydesk-setup.exe","anydeskmsi.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","SyncFuture.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ (LegitInstallers)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files"
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LegitInstallers = dynamic(["msiexec.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe","explorer.exe","services.exe","wusa.exe","trustedinstaller.exe","anydesk-setup.exe","anydeskmsi.exe"]);
let TargetChildren = dynamic(["anydesk.exe","syncfuture.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ChildBin = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend ParentBin = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where ChildBin in (TargetChildren)
| where not (ParentBin in (LegitInstallers))
| where not (ParentProcessName startswith @"C:\Program Files")
| where not (ParentProcessName startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: AnyDesk or SyncFuture Spawned from Non-Installer Parent
id: ace5d6f7-4567-4a9a-bcde-f01234567890
description: Detects AnyDesk.exe or SyncFuture.exe being launched by a parent process that is NOT a legitimate installer / Windows service / Program Files binary. Maps to TA4922 RomulusLoader RMM-deployment pattern from Proofpoint June 2026.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/china-linked-ta4922-expands-phishing.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1219
  - attack.t1574.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AnyDesk.exe'
      - '\SyncFuture.exe'
  filter_installer_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\setup.exe'
      - '\installer.exe'
      - '\explorer.exe'
      - '\services.exe'
      - '\wusa.exe'
      - '\TrustedInstaller.exe'
      - '\AnyDesk-Setup.exe'
      - '\AnyDeskMSI.exe'
  filter_program_files:
    ParentImage|startswith:
      - 'C:\Program Files\'
      - 'C:\Program Files (x86)\'
  condition: selection_child and not (filter_installer_parent or filter_program_files)
falsepositives:
  - Approved IT-managed AnyDesk deployment via custom wrapper (whitelist the wrapper)
  - SCCM / Intune managed-app deployment via non-standard agent
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @Image:(*\AnyDesk.exe OR *\anydesk.exe OR *\ANYDESK.EXE OR *\SyncFuture.exe OR *\syncfuture.exe OR *\SYNCFUTURE.EXE) -@ParentImage:(*\msiexec.exe OR *\MSIEXEC.EXE OR *\setup.exe OR *\Setup.exe OR *\installer.exe OR *\Installer.exe OR *\explorer.exe OR *\Explorer.exe OR *\EXPLORER.EXE OR *\services.exe OR *\Services.exe OR *\wusa.exe OR *\TrustedInstaller.exe OR *\AnyDesk-Setup.exe OR *\AnyDeskMSI.exe OR *"\Program Files\"* OR *"\Program Files (x86)\"*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(AnyDesk|SyncFuture)\.exe$/i
| NOT ParentBaseFileName=/^(msiexec|setup|installer|explorer|services|wusa|TrustedInstaller|AnyDesk[-_]?Setup|AnyDeskMSI)\.exe$/i
| NOT ParentImageFileName=/\\Program Files( \(x86\))?\\/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| search NOT (parent_process_name IN ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","installer.exe","explorer.exe","services.exe","wusa.exe","TrustedInstaller.exe","AnyDesk-Setup.exe","AnyDeskMSI.exe"))

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_process values(Processes.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","SyncFuture.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path Processes.parent_process_path

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\SplashtopStreamer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Remote-Management (RMM) Tool Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0c
status: experimental
description: |
    AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera / Splashtop /
    RustDesk — RMM tools attackers commonly install for hands-on-
    keyboard access. Filter against the IT estate's known tool.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1219/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1219
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\AnyDesk.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer.exe'
            - '\TeamViewer_Service.exe'
            - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
            - '\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe'
            - '\atera_agent.exe'
            - '\SplashtopStreamer.exe'
            - '\RustDesk.exe'
            - '\NinjaOne.exe'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - IT-approved RMM in use across the estate. Maintain a known-IT-
      tool exclusion list per environment.
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe","kaseya*.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("Consent to application.","Add OAuth2PermissionGrant.","Add delegated permission grant.")
| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,
          ActivityObjects, IPAddress, UserAgent
// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),
         AppId   = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].id),
         User    = tostring(parse_json(tostring(InitiatedBy)).user.userPrincipalName)
| project TimeGenerated, OperationName, User, AppName, AppId, Result
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application

    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    product: azure
    service: auditlogs

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688

| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

DeviceNetworkEvents

union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Likely
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hypotheses, telemetry, and human judgment: Inside Cisco Talos Threat Hunting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest dropping script.ps1 to user AppData (KongTuke stage-2)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path · [LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
[LLM] KongTuke TDS C2 callout to 144.31.221.82:6060 with /capcha URL path Command & Control High
Hunts the specific KongTuke (TAG-124 / 404 TDS) command-and-control infrastructure named in the Talos case study: outbound HTTP to 144.31.221.82 on TCP/6060 with a URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint. Single-IOC alerting because all three values are article-named. Rationale: Single high-confidence IOC bundle straight from the Talos case-study paragraph: IP 144.31.221.82, TCP/6060, URL path /capcha9856. The /capcha* fingerprint is corroborated by Recorded Future (TAG-124), Red Canary KongTuke profile, and malware-traffic-analysis.net Jan 2026 KongTuke ClickFix capture. Cross-checked via WebSearch — KongTuke is a real, active TDS. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base • https://www.malware-traffic-analysis.net/2026/01/08/index.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002

title: KongTuke TDS C2 to 144.31.221.82 / capcha URL Path
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a01
description: Detects outbound network traffic to KongTuke TDS C2 infrastructure (144.31.221.82:6060) or any URL path matching the KongTuke /capcha* fingerprint reported by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
  - https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base

date: 2026/06/04
tags:

  - attack.command_and_control

  category: network_connection
  product: windows

  selection_ip:
    DestinationIp: '144.31.221.82'
  selection_port_path:
    DestinationPort: 6060
    DestinationHostname|contains: '/capcha'
  selection_path:
    Url|contains: '/capcha9856'
  condition: selection_ip or selection_port_path or selection_path
falsepositives:
  - None expected; this IP/port/path combination has no known legitimate use.
level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 OR source:cisco-firepower OR source:cisco_secure_firewall) AND (@DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 OR (@DestinationPort:6060 AND @DestinationHostname:*\/capcha*) OR @network.destination.ip:144.31.221.82 OR @url:*\/capcha9856*)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 (RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82" OR RemotePort=6060)

[LLM] PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest dropping script.ps1 to user AppData (KongTuke stage-2) Installation Medium
Hunts the KongTuke stage-2 download pattern from the Talos case study: a powershell.exe process whose command line invokes Invoke-WebRequest (or iwr) and writes a file named script.ps1 into the user's ApplicationData / AppData directory. Pairs the URL-fetch verb, the article-named filename, and the article-named drop location in one event. Rationale: The combination of three article-named tokens in one PowerShell command line — Invoke-WebRequest verb, exact filename script.ps1, and AppData/ApplicationData drop path — collapses to one cmdline-substring detection that's high specificity. Sourced directly from the Talos KongTuke walk-through (cmd.exe → powershell.exe -EncodedCommand → IWR → script.ps1 → ApplicationData). Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/ • https://www.recordedfuture.com/research/tag-124-multi-layered-tds-infrastructure-extensive-user-base

title: KongTuke PowerShell Drops script.ps1 to AppData via Invoke-WebRequest
id: 7e3b1f4e-1f0e-4a2e-9b8d-6b1f4e3c2a02
description: Detects PowerShell command line that fetches a remote file named script.ps1 and writes it into the user's AppData directory — the KongTuke stage-2 download chain documented by Cisco Talos.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/hypotheses-telemetry-and-human-judgment-inside-cisco-talos-threat-hunting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
  selection_fetch:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
      - 'iwr '
      - 'Net.WebClient'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'DownloadString'
  selection_file:
    CommandLine|contains: 'script.ps1'
  selection_path:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'AppData'
      - 'ApplicationData'
      - '\Roaming\'
      - '\Local\'
  condition: all of selection_*
falsepositives:
  - Legitimate internal scripts that happen to fetch a file named script.ps1 into AppData (rare; review user context)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe)) AND (@CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *iwr\ * OR *Net.WebClient* OR *DownloadFile* OR *DownloadString*)) AND @CommandLine:*script.ps1* AND (@CommandLine:(*AppData* OR *ApplicationData* OR *\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Local\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh)\.exe$/i
| regex("(Invoke-WebRequest|iwr |Net\.WebClient|DownloadFile|DownloadString)", field=CommandLine)
| regex("script\.ps1", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(AppData|ApplicationData|\\\\Roaming\\\\|\\\\Local\\\\)", field=CommandLine)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdlines values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parents from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") (Processes.process="*Invoke-WebRequest*" OR Processes.process="*iwr *" OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*") Processes.process="*script.ps1*" (Processes.process="*AppData*" OR Processes.process="*ApplicationData*" OR Processes.process="*\\Roaming\\*" OR Processes.process="*\\Local\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`

[LLM] Same host calling KongTuke C2 from both powershell.exe and curl.exe within short window Command & Control High
Reproduces the Talos multi-source-correlation insight: the same endpoint reaching 144.31.221.82 from two distinct binaries (powershell.exe via Invoke-WebRequest and curl.exe directly) is the disambiguating signal that turned a single firewall hit into a confirmed intrusion. Single-binary callouts to the IP are already caught by UC1; this UC fires on the host-level fan-out only. Rationale: Directly encodes the Talos case-study insight: 'a separate curl.exe process making requests to the same C2 infrastructure the firewall had flagged.' Two distinct LOLBin/native binaries calling the same KongTuke IP from one host is high-fidelity even without the URL-path filter — it's the multi-process fan-out that confirms intrusion vs single-shot scanning. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/threat-detection-report/threats/kongtuke/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP == "144.31.221.82" or (RemotePort == 6060 and RemoteUrl has "/capcha")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "curl.exe")
| summarize ProcessSet = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName),
            FirstConnection = min(Timestamp),
            LastConnection = max(Timestamp),
            ConnectionCount = count(),
            CmdLines = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 8)
          by DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteIP, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where array_length(ProcessSet) >= 2
| where (ProcessSet has "curl.exe") and (ProcessSet has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe"))
| order by FirstConnection desc
let WindowHours = 1h;
let FirewallHits = CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where DestinationIP == "144.31.221.82" or (DestinationPort == 6060 and RequestURL has "/capcha")
    | project FirewallTime=TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL;
let ProcessHits = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\powershell.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\pwsh.exe"
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | where CommandLine has_any ("144.31.221.82", "capcha", "script.ps1")
         or NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe"
    | project ProcessTime=TimeGenerated, Computer, NewProcessName, CommandLine, SubjectUserName;
FirewallHits
| join kind=inner (
    ProcessHits
    | summarize Procs=make_set(NewProcessName), AnyCmd=make_set(CommandLine, 8) by Computer
    | where array_length(Procs) >= 2
) on $left.SourceIP == $right.Computer
| order by FirewallTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:144.31.221.82 @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\Curl.exe OR *\\CURL.EXE)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="144.31.221.82"
| ContextImageFileName=/(powershell|pwsh|curl)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=[collect([ContextImageFileName]), count(), min(@timestamp), max(@timestamp)])
| length(ContextImageFileName) >= 2

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

According to Palo Alto Networks Unit 42, the campaign is said to be the next stage of a previously reported activity cluster dubbed JSCoreRunner (aka FileRipple) in late August 2025. [LLM] Chrome Preferences tamper on macOS by non-Chrome process (FlutterShell browser hijack) Installation High
FlutterShell rewrites Google Chrome configuration files on macOS to force traffic through an attacker-controlled ad-intermediary site. This hunts writes to Chrome's Preferences/Local State by any process other than Chrome itself, which is the article-specific browser-hijack tell. Rationale: Anchors on the article's most specific operational behaviour: "modifies Google Chrome configuration files to hijack the browser, forcing all traffic through an attacker-controlled, ad-filled intermediary site." Filtering for non-Chrome writers eliminates almost all baseline Chrome self-writes. Cross-checked against Unit 42 / Palo Alto Networks blog coverage of JSCoreRunner/FileRipple. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
ATT&CKT1176 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FolderPath has "/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/"
| where FileName in~ ("Preferences","Secure Preferences","Local State")

[LLM] macOS host beaconing to FlutterShell C2 / ad-intermediary domains Command & Control High
Hunts DNS resolution or network connections from macOS endpoints to the article's named FlutterShell infrastructure (ads-parkpro/adsparkpro/softwe.art front-company domains plus the four C2 cover domains). High-fidelity given the IOCs come straight from Unit 42's IOC list and are unlikely to appear in any legitimate macOS workload. Rationale: Direct match on Unit 42's named infrastructure for Operation FlutterBridge. Domains correspond to article-stated front companies (AdsParkPro LTD, SOFT WE ART LIMITED) and C2 cover. Domains have no legitimate use in any enterprise; one hit warrants an alert. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://urlhaus.abuse.ch/

[LLM] Known FlutterShell SHA256 binary execution on macOS Installation High
Direct hash-match alert on the eight FlutterShell SHA256s published by Unit 42 for the PodcastsLounge / PDF-Brain / PDF-Ninja variants. Defender XDR + Sentinel + Falcon all surface SHA256 on process telemetry — minimum-friction high-fidelity tripwire for in-the-wild samples. Rationale: Unit 42 IOC SHA256s are tier-1 confidence and shared across three FlutterShell variants. Notarized signing means file-reputation alone won't catch these; hash-match is the cleanest tripwire. Cross-referenced against Unit 42 IOC bundle. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://www.virustotal.com/

[LLM] FlutterShell WebView bridge spawns shell on macOS (arbitrary command execution capability) Actions on Objectives Medium
FlutterShell uses a JavaScript-to-native bridge inside a WebView to invoke shell commands on demand from attacker-controlled JavaScript. Hunts macOS Flutter-style apps (signed with the article's known shell-company developers, or matching the named variant binary names) spawning /bin/sh, /bin/bash, /usr/bin/zsh, /usr/bin/osascript — the smoking-gun behaviour of the JS-bridge backdoor. Rationale: Anchors on the article's three named variant binaries (PodcastsLounge, PDF-Brain, PDF-Ninja) AND the WebView-JS-bridge architecture that necessitates spawning a shell to execute attacker-supplied commands. A legitimate PDF reader or podcast app has no reason to fork /bin/sh. The signer-name pivot (AdsParkPro / Advantage Web Marketing / SOFT WE ART / PACIFIC TRADE SOLUTIONS) catches future variants that change the binary name. Cross-checked against: • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(60d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("PodcastsLounge","PDF-Brain","PDF-Ninja")
   or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any ("/PodcastsLounge.app/","/PDF-Brain.app/","/PDF-Ninja.app/")
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("AdsParkPro","Advantage Web Marketing","SOFT WE ART","PACIFIC TRADE SOLUTIONS")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","zsh","dash","osascript","curl","python","python3","env")
| extend HasShellArgs = ProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","-c\"","-e ","do shell script","printenv","env")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessSHA256, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, HasShellArgs
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(60d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("PodcastsLounge","PDF-Brain","PDF-Ninja")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("/PodcastsLounge.app/","/PDF-Brain.app/","/PDF-Ninja.app/")
   or ActingProcessFileCompany has_any ("AdsParkPro","Advantage Web Marketing","SOFT WE ART","PACIFIC TRADE SOLUTIONS")
| where TargetProcessName has_any ("/bin/sh","/bin/bash","/bin/zsh","/bin/dash","/usr/bin/osascript","/usr/bin/curl","/usr/bin/python","/usr/bin/python3","/usr/bin/env")
| extend HasShellArgs = TargetProcessCommandLine has_any ("-c ","do shell script","printenv","env")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessFileCompany, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, HasShellArgs, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
