title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("atsheisdomestic.org", "etoftheappyrince.org", "healightejustb.org", "sinterfumesco.com", "ads-parkpro.com", "adsparkpro.top", "adsparkpro.net", "softwe.art")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or SHA1 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or MD5 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or SHA1 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745") or MD5 in~ ("021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["021666417de8b9972c179783fe60d4c4ad2d93224e3a0f16137065c960b1b845", "363923500ce942bf1a953e8a4e943fbf1fb1b5ed6e5d247964c345b3ad5bfc34", "8421c902364980e3d762ec6dbbe6b0f40577c27bd79b48c57d098328b2533109", "644fc49fa1006a2a2acace694e5fb83753164e2617051ece6d9dc9ea32329e70", "9053e8ddaecca1f960c041c944ca8799fc71dc86a4b50d2639ee4e0d2cb82f47", "b60074d1ea2008a581f432f2dee5f84f78668d9dd8e66f75d03c42dabd89bdea", "9425e8e39fa8a7212cdd07f0917cb3dfde38a90b87297de2c82a5850aff1e4de", "30448686ec900d5213d74f08f0d2b7924c5336a29445b2a434aba8d8b19d7530", "48047c34bfd57fe1e24bc538bc2ce9e0ac4c4eb48d3b0c195b414f0379dc0745"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Suspicious HTTP request to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer endpoint (CVE-2026-20230 exploitation)
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Anomalous outbound HTTP from Cisco Unified CM appliance (post-CVE-2026-20230 SSRF callback)
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
[LLM] Suspicious HTTP request to Cisco Unified CM WebDialer endpoint (CVE-2026-20230 exploitation) Exploitation Medium
Hunts for crafted HTTP requests targeting the Cisco Unified CM WebDialer service that may exploit CVE-2026-20230 SSRF. WebDialer is the only vulnerable component per Cisco's advisory; requests to its endpoints from non-Jabber clients are high-fidelity probe/exploit signals while a patch is pending. Rationale: Cisco PSIRT advisory states WebDialer is the only vulnerable service and the SSRF requires a crafted HTTP request to its endpoint. Filtering on WebDialer URL fragments + excluding legitimate Cisco UC clients yields high-fidelity exploitation candidates. Cross-checked with Cisco security advisory for CVE-2026-20230 referenced in article. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/publicationListing.x • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisco-warns-of-critical-unified-cm-flaw-with-poc-exploit-code/
ATT&CKT1190 T1090
Data sourcesWeb.Web
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemotePort in (8080, 8443, 443)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("webdialer", "WebDialer", "makeCallProxy", "cucm-uds", "CCMCIP")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ciscojabber.exe", "cipc.exe", "finesse.exe", "outlook.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe", "msedge.exe", "firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl", "python", "powershell", "-X POST", "-X PUT")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort
| order by Timestamp desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort in (8080, 8443, 443)
| where isnotempty(RequestURL)
| where RequestURL has_any ("webdialer", "WebDialer", "makeCallProxy", "cucm-uds", "CCMCIP")
| where RequestMethod in~ ("POST", "PUT", "GET")
| where RequestClientApplication !has_any ("CiscoJabber", "CiscoIPCommunicator", "Finesse", "CiscoSystems")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL, RequestMethod, RequestClientApplication
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] Anomalous outbound HTTP from Cisco Unified CM appliance (post-CVE-2026-20230 SSRF callback) Command & Control Medium
Hunts for outbound HTTP(S) connections originating from the Cisco Unified CM appliance to non-Cisco destinations. CVE-2026-20230 is an SSRF that may pivot to fetch a second-stage file dropper; CUCM appliances normally egress only to Cisco update/licensing infrastructure. Rationale: CVE-2026-20230 is server-side request forgery — successful exploitation will cause the CUCM appliance itself to initiate outbound HTTP to fetch a payload. CUCMs have a tightly-scoped egress profile (Cisco/Webex/licensing/SMTP), so any other destination is anomalous. Cross-checked Cisco PSIRT advisory for CVE-2026-20230. Cross-checked against: • https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/publicationListing.x • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/cisco-warns-of-critical-unified-cm-flaw-with-poc-exploit-code/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents

| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")

LSASS process access / dump (credential theft) Actions on Objectives High
Mimikatz, comsvcs.dll MiniDump, or any non-Windows process opening LSASS.
ATT&CKT1003.001 T1003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceEvents
DeviceEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType == "OpenProcessApiCall"
| where FileName =~ "lsass.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","MsMpEng.exe","csrss.exe",
                                          "svchost.exe","wininit.exe","services.exe",
                                          "lsm.exe","SearchProtocolHost.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, AccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
// SecurityEvent EventID 4663 = object access. AccessMask 0x10 / 0x40 / 0x1010
// indicate read access to lsass.exe — credential-dump signature. Audit
// Object Access > Audit File System policy required.
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4663
| where ObjectName endswith "\lsass.exe"
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ObjectName, ProcessName,
          AccessMask, AccessReason
| order by TimeGenerated desc

The Hacker News
2026-06-04 15 use cases 9 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

"The sites are well-designed and often look like legitimate project portals at a glance, sometimes referencing

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Outbound contact to fake open-source tool / TDS / CloudFront staging domains · [LLM] Browser-spawned executable/installer drop within 5 min of TDS site contact · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] AnimateClipper ClickFix paste-to-run via explorer.exe spawning mshta/powershell/cmd · Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SessionGate final-stage rundll32 spawning cmd.exe to fetch and silently execute next-stage payload · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Remus/Lumma Stealer browser-credential and crypto-wallet directory enumeration · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Outbound contact to fake open-source tool / TDS / CloudFront staging domains Delivery High
Detects host or browser contact (DNS or HTTP) with the eight typosquatted Ghidra/dnSpy/SpiderFoot/grpcurl lookalike sites and the CloudFront-hosted staging layer + downstream TDS endpoints used to deliver SessionGate, Remus Stealer and AnimateClipper. Rationale: Eight domains pulled verbatim from the Check Point breakdown / pre-extracted IOC block (grpcurl.com, ghidralite.com, two CloudFront staging hosts, plus four TDS endpoints). All are confirmed by Check Point and the November 2025 Fullstory write-up referenced in the article body — high-fidelity atomic IOCs. logsource:
  category: dns
detection:

    QueryName:

      - 'ghidralite.com'
      - 'dcbbwymp1bhif.cloudfront.net'
      - 'd3jzqhqvnvdy34.cloudfront.net'
      - 'oundhertobeconisist.org'
      - 'trkscope.xyz'

level: high

[LLM] Browser-spawned executable/installer drop within 5 min of TDS site contact Delivery High
Time-window correlation between a browser visit to a TDS / fake-tool domain and a fresh .exe/.msi/.dll/.zip dropped into Downloads/Temp by that same browser process. Catches the click-handoff step where the CloudFront JS staging layer converts a 'Download' click into a TDS-gated payload. Rationale: The article describes the 'Download' button click as a click-interception handoff via CloudFront JS to a TDS. A 5-minute browser→file-drop window keyed off contact with one of the 8 named domains converts the noisy 'browser dropped a file' signal into a high-fidelity TDS-delivery signal. Cross-checked against: • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/ • https://www.fullstory.com/blog/
ATT&CKT1189 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Web.Web
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TDSDomains = dynamic(["grpcurl.com","ghidralite.com","dcbbwymp1bhif.cloudfront.net","d3jzqhqvnvdy34.cloudfront.net","oundhertobeconisist.org","trkscope.xyz","file-enter-web.com","realcubeoyogenmyfire.monster"]);
let TDSTouches = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (TDSDomains)
  | project TouchTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, RemoteUrl;
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".msi" or FileName endswith ".dll" or FileName endswith ".zip" or FileName endswith ".js"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| join kind=inner TDSTouches on DeviceId
| where Timestamp between (TouchTime .. TouchTime + 5m)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, FileOriginUrl, RemoteUrl, TouchTime
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let TDSDomains = dynamic(["grpcurl.com","ghidralite.com","dcbbwymp1bhif.cloudfront.net","d3jzqhqvnvdy34.cloudfront.net","oundhertobeconisist.org","trkscope.xyz","file-enter-web.com","realcubeoyogenmyfire.monster"]);
let TDSTouches = ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
  | where Url has_any (TDSDomains) or DstHostname has_any (TDSDomains)
  | project TouchTime=TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Url;
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Downloads\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\")
| where TargetFileExtension in~ ("exe","msi","dll","zip","js","msix")
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| join kind=inner TDSTouches on DvcHostname
| where TimeGenerated between (TouchTime .. TouchTime + 5m)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, Url
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\opera.exe) @TargetFilename:(*\\Downloads\\* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\*) @TargetFilename:(*.exe OR *.msi OR *.dll OR *.zip OR *.js)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten ContextImageFileName=/(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|opera)\.exe$/i TargetFileName=/\\(Downloads|Temp|Roaming)\\.+\.(exe|msi|dll|zip|js)$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/^(grpcurl\.com|ghidralite\.com|dcbbwymp1bhif\.cloudfront\.net|d3jzqhqvnvdy34\.cloudfront\.net|oundhertobeconisist\.org|trkscope\.xyz|file-enter-web\.com|realcubeoyogenmyfire\.monster)$/i | tail(1)}, field=aid, include=[DomainName, ContextProcessId])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName, DomainName], function=count())

[LLM] SessionGate final-stage rundll32 spawning cmd.exe to fetch and silently execute next-stage payload Installation High
Detects the SessionGate end-of-chain behaviour described in the article: a DLL loaded via rundll32.exe spawning cmd.exe to download and silently execute the unique-per-client next-stage malware. Specifically targets rundll32 living under user-writable paths (\AppData\, \Users\Public\) with cmd.exe carrying URL / download-utility tokens. Rationale: The article explicitly states the final DLL '...downloading and silently executing the next-stage malware via cmd.exe.' Pinning the detection on rundll32→cmd.exe with download-utility tokens or a user-writable parent path is article-specific and not covered by generic rundll32 abuse rules. The legitimate-pattern allowlist (printui, Control_RunDLL, mshtml PrintHTML) is the standard suppressor. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1218/011/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/
ATT&CKT1218.011 T1059.003 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "rundll32.exe"
| where FileName =~ "cmd.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","curl ","certutil","bitsadmin","powershell","Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\")
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("printui.dll","shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL","mshtml.dll,PrintHTML"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\rundll32.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\cmd.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","curl ","certutil","bitsadmin","powershell","Invoke-WebRequest","iwr ")
   or ParentProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\Users\Public\")
| where not(ParentProcessName has_any ("printui.dll","Control_RunDLL"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SessionGate rundll32 Spawning cmd.exe With Download Utility From User-Writable Path
id: 8b4f3c2d-7e2a-4d1b-a3c2-1f4d6e7a8b9c
description: Detects the SessionGate end-stage chain where a DLL loaded via rundll32 from AppData/Users\Public spawns cmd.exe to fetch and silently execute the next-stage payload.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/fake-sites-mimicking-open-source-tools.html

logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\rundll32.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith: '\cmd.exe'
  selection_context:
    - CommandLine|contains:
        - 'http://'
        - 'https://'
        - 'curl '
        - 'certutil'
        - 'bitsadmin'
        - 'powershell'
        - 'Invoke-WebRequest'
    - ParentCommandLine|contains:
        - '\AppData\Local\Temp\'
        - '\AppData\Roaming\'
        - '\Users\Public\'
  filter_legit:
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - 'printui.dll'
      - 'shell32.dll,Control_RunDLL'
      - 'mshtml.dll,PrintHTML'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_context and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\rundll32.exe OR *\\RUNDLL32.EXE) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE) AND (@CommandLine:(*http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/* OR *curl* OR *certutil* OR *bitsadmin* OR *powershell* OR *Invoke-WebRequest*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/rundll32\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\cmd\.exe$/i
| (regex("(?i)(http://|https://|curl |certutil|bitsadmin|powershell|Invoke-WebRequest|iwr )", field=CommandLine) OR regex("(?i)\\\\(AppData\\\\(Local|Roaming)|Users\\\\Public)\\\\", field=ParentCommandLine))
| NOT regex("(?i)(printui\.dll|shell32\.dll,Control_RunDLL|mshtml\.dll,PrintHTML)", field=ParentCommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

[LLM] Remus/Lumma Stealer browser-credential and crypto-wallet directory enumeration Actions on Objectives Medium
Hunts for a single non-browser process touching three or more files across Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Brave Login Data stores AND/OR Exodus/Electrum/Atomic/Ledger Live/Coinomi/Bitcoin/Zcash wallet directories. Targets the Remus Stealer behaviour (article: 'steal data from more than 20 browsers...cryptocurrency wallets, two-factor authentication tools, and password managers'). Rationale: Article explicitly lists Remus Stealer's targets: 'more than 20 browsers, hundreds of browser extensions and applications, cryptocurrency wallets, two-factor authentication tools, and password managers'. The composite test — same non-browser process touching ≥3 distinct credential/wallet artefacts in a short window — is the canonical stealer fan-out signature and is robust to whichever variant of Remus/Lumma is delivered. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1167/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
let WindowDays = 7d;
let WalletPaths = dynamic([@"\AppData\Roaming\Exodus\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Electrum\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Atomic\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Ledger Live\",@"\AppData\Local\Coinomi\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Zcash\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Bitcoin\"]);
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles",@"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\Default\Login Data"]);
let LegitProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","explorer.exe","SearchIndexer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","svchost.exe","Bitwarden.exe","1Password.exe"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(WindowDays)
| where FolderPath has_any (WalletPaths) or FolderPath has_any (CredPaths)
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ (LegitProcs))
| summarize FilesTouched=dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            SamplePaths=make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 10),
            FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where FilesTouched >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let WindowDays = 7d;
let WalletPaths = dynamic([@"\AppData\Roaming\Exodus\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Electrum\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Atomic\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Ledger Live\",@"\AppData\Local\Coinomi\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Zcash\",@"\AppData\Roaming\Bitcoin\"]);
let CredPaths = dynamic([@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Login Data",@"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles",@"\BraveSoftware\Brave-Browser\User Data\Default\Login Data"]);
let LegitProcs = dynamic(["chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","explorer.exe","SearchIndexer.exe","MsMpEng.exe","svchost.exe","Bitwarden.exe","1Password.exe"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
| where TargetFilePath has_any (WalletPaths) or TargetFilePath has_any (CredPaths)
| where not(ActingProcessName in~ (LegitProcs))
| summarize FilesTouched=dcount(TargetFilePath),
            SamplePaths=make_set(TargetFilePath, 10),
            FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| where FilesTouched >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:(11 OR 23) @TargetFilename:(*\\AppData\\Roaming\\Exodus\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Electrum\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Atomic\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Ledger?Live\\* OR *\\AppData\\Local\\Coinomi\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Zcash\\* OR *\\AppData\\Roaming\\Bitcoin\\* OR *\\Chrome\\User?Data\\Default\\Login?Data* OR *\\Edge\\User?Data\\Default\\Login?Data* OR *\\Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles* OR *\\Brave-Browser\\User?Data\\Default\\Login?Data*) -@Image:(*\\chrome.exe OR *\\msedge.exe OR *\\firefox.exe OR *\\brave.exe OR *\\explorer.exe OR *\\SearchIndexer.exe OR *\\MsMpEng.exe)
#event_simpleName=/^(FileWritten|FileOpenInfo)$/ TargetFileName=/\\(AppData\\(Roaming|Local)\\(Exodus|Electrum|Atomic|Ledger Live|Coinomi|Zcash|Bitcoin)|Chrome\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data|Edge\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data|Mozilla\\Firefox\\Profiles|Brave-Browser\\User Data\\Default\\Login Data)/i
| NOT ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|explorer|SearchIndexer|MsMpEng|svchost)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=FilesTouched))
| FilesTouched >= 3

[LLM] AnimateClipper ClickFix paste-to-run via explorer.exe spawning mshta/powershell/cmd Exploitation High
Detects the ClickFix delivery pattern used by AnimateClipper where the lure tricks the user into pasting a malicious command into the Windows Run dialog, producing an explorer.exe → mshta.exe/powershell.exe/cmd.exe chain carrying URL or base64 tokens. Pinned to the clipboard-paste characteristics described in the article. Rationale: Article calls out AnimateClipper as 'delivered by means of a ClickFix lure'. ClickFix's canonical artefact is explorer.exe (the Run-dialog host) as parent of an interpreter or LOLBin with a URL or base64-encoded payload on the cmd line — a tight signature that is article-specific, not the generic encoded-PowerShell rule. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/004/ • https://research.checkpoint.com/2026/
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001 T1218.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "explorer.exe"
| where FileName in~ ("mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","FromBase64String","DownloadString","DownloadFile","IEX","Invoke-Expression","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","javascript:","mshtml:","Set-Clipboard","hidden")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\explorer.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\mshta.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\cmd.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("http://","https://","FromBase64String","DownloadString","DownloadFile","IEX","Invoke-Expression","-EncodedCommand","-enc ","javascript:","mshtml:","Set-Clipboard","hidden")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\explorer.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'FromBase64String'
      - 'DownloadString'
      - 'DownloadFile'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'Invoke-Expression'
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc '
      - 'javascript:'
      - 'mshtml:'
      - 'Set-Clipboard'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\explorer.exe OR *\\EXPLORER.EXE) @Image:(*\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe) @CommandLine:(*http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/* OR *FromBase64String* OR *DownloadString* OR *DownloadFile* OR *IEX* OR *Invoke-Expression* OR *-EncodedCommand* OR *javascript\:* OR *mshtml\:* OR *Set-Clipboard*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/explorer\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\(mshta|powershell|pwsh|cmd|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| regex("(?i)(https?://|FromBase64String|DownloadString|DownloadFile|IEX|Invoke-Expression|-EncodedCommand|-enc |javascript:|mshtml:|Set-Clipboard)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" (Processes.process_name IN ("mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")) (Processes.process IN ("*http://*","*https://*","*FromBase64String*","*DownloadString*","*DownloadFile*","*IEX*","*Invoke-Expression*","*-EncodedCommand*","*-enc *","*javascript:*","*mshtml:*","*Set-Clipboard*")) BY Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count, min(_time) as firstTime, max(_time) as lastTime FROM datamodel=Endpoint.Processes WHERE Processes.parent_process_name="explorer.exe" (Processes.process_name IN ("mshta.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")) (Processes.process IN ("*http://*","*https://*","*FromBase64String*","*DownloadString*","*DownloadFile*","*IEX*","*Invoke-Expression*","*-EncodedCommand*","*-enc *","*javascript:*","*mshtml:*","*Set-Clipboard*")) BY Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process, Processes.process, Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Suspicious browser extension installation Installation Medium
Side-loaded / unsigned extensions, often masquerading as wallets, productivity tools.
ATT&CKT1176
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry DeviceRegistryEvents
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any ("\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\","\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\","\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where RegistryKey has_any (@"\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\",
                              @"\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey,
          RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |
    Registry writes under the browser extension policy keys —
    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /
    info-stealers to bypass user-level extension controls.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1176/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1176
    - attack.persistence
logsource:
    category: registry_event
    product: windows
detection:
    selection:
        TargetObject|contains:
            - '\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\'
            - '\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\'
    condition: selection
falsepositives:
    - Group-policy-managed extension whitelists
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry
    where (Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Google\Chrome\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Microsoft\Edge\Extensions\*"
        OR Registry.registry_path="*\Software\Mozilla\Firefox\Extensions\*")
    by Registry.dest, Registry.registry_path, Registry.registry_value_data, Registry.registry_value_name, Registry.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)`
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false count

         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")

     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\winword.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\powerpnt.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\outlook.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\onenote.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\mspub.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\visio.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\winword.exe'
            - '\excel.exe'
            - '\powerpnt.exe'
            - '\outlook.exe'
            - '\onenote.exe'
            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
    - Legitimate automation macros in trusted internal documents
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe","outlook.exe","onenote.exe","mspub.exe","visio.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

High

Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months

The Hacker News
2026-06-04 14 use cases 6 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

Unknown attackers spent at least five months inside the Outlook mailbox of a senior executive at a major global stock exchange, copying the inbox out in small, repeated batches and routing it through Dropbox and OneDrive so the traffic blended into normal cloud activity. Symantec and Carbon Black's Threat Hunter Team reported the campaign this week. This points to espionage, not a money grab:

ATT&CKT1053.005 T1190 T1195.002 T1528 T1555.003 T1566
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
