Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Hackers Spied on a Stock Exchange Executive's Outlook Mailbox for Five Months
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Aspose.Email/Aspose.Pst mailbox library loaded by non-Outlook process · [LLM] Scheduled task masquerading as Adobe/Lenovo/OneDrive system service · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] FRPC (Fast Reverse Proxy client) execution by config-file argument
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] PST exported by non-Outlook binary with password and date-range CLI flags · [LLM] curl/non-browser binary uploading to Dropbox or OneDrive personal API endpoints · Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
[LLM] Aspose.Email/Aspose.Pst mailbox library loaded by non-Outlook process Installation High
Hunts for the Aspose .NET library — which the Symantec/Carbon Black report identifies as the core of the attacker's mailbox stealer — being loaded by any process other than legitimate Outlook utilities. Aspose.Email and Aspose.Pst are the modules that read OST and write PST; their use outside Outlook/scanpst is highly anomalous on an executive endpoint. Rationale: Aspose.Email/Aspose.Pst are the specific libraries the article names as the heart of the mailbox stealer; loading them outside Outlook/scanpst is high-fidelity. Cross-checked Aspose product naming on the vendor site and Symantec's WastedLocker/Cl0p style write-ups, which use the same library identifiers. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.aspose.com/email/net/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/001/
ATT&CKT1114.001 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName has_any ("Aspose.Email", "Aspose.Pst") or FolderPath has_any ("Aspose.Email", "Aspose.Pst")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("outlook.exe", "scanpst.exe", "scanost.exe", "olmapi32.dll")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
WindowsEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 7
| where EventData has_any ("Aspose.Email", "Aspose.Pst")
| where EventData !has "OUTLOOK.EXE" and EventData !has "scanpst.exe" and EventData !has "scanost.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Provider, EventID, EventData
title: Aspose Mailbox Library Loaded by Non-Outlook Process
id: 5c7d2e3a-9b4f-4a12-bd1a-1c2e3f4a5b6c
description: Detects Aspose.Email or Aspose.Pst .NET libraries being loaded by a process other than Outlook or PST repair tools, a signature behaviour of the stock-exchange-executive mailbox stealer reported by Symantec.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hackers-spied-on-stock-exchange.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1114.001
  - attack.t1005
logsource:
  category: image_load
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ImageLoaded|contains:
      - 'Aspose.Email'
      - 'Aspose.Pst'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\scanpst.exe'
      - '\scanost.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Third-party mail-archive / e-discovery tools (Veritas, MailStore) that legitimately use Aspose
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:7 (@ImageLoaded:(*Aspose.Email* OR *aspose.email* OR *Aspose.Pst* OR *aspose.pst*)) -@Image:(*\\outlook.exe OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\\scanpst.exe OR *\\scanost.exe)
#event_simpleName=ClassifiedModuleLoad OR #event_simpleName=ImageHash
| ImageFileName=/(Aspose\.Email|Aspose\.Pst)/i
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\\(outlook|scanpst|scanost)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, ImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name!=outlook.exe Processes.process_name!=scanpst.exe Processes.process_name!=scanost.exe (Processes.process IN ("*Aspose.Email*","*Aspose.Pst*") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*Aspose.Email*","*Aspose.Pst*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name!=outlook.exe Processes.process_name!=scanpst.exe Processes.process_name!=scanost.exe (Processes.process IN ("*Aspose.Email*","*Aspose.Pst*") OR Processes.parent_process IN ("*Aspose.Email*","*Aspose.Pst*")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
[LLM] PST exported by non-Outlook binary with password and date-range CLI flags Actions on Objectives High
Detects file writes of .pst files by a process that is not Outlook/scanpst when the launching command line carries password or date-range arguments. This is the article-specific operational pattern: the attacker's Aspose-wrapped tool was 'run each time with a password and a date-range flag' to slice the mailbox into bi-weekly chunks. Rationale: Both the file shape (.pst created by a non-Outlook process) and the CLI argument shape (password + date range) come directly from the article's description of how the attacker ran the tool eight times between Nov 2025 and Feb 2026. The combination is what makes it high-fidelity — either signal alone is too noisy. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1114/001/
ATT&CKT1114.001 T1560.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName endswith ".pst"
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("outlook.exe", "scanpst.exe", "scanost.exe", "olmapi32.dll")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-password", "/password", "-pwd", "/pwd", "-startdate", "-enddate", "/startdate", "/enddate", "-from", "-to", "-range", "/range", "-since")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName endswith ".pst"
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("outlook.exe", "scanpst.exe", "scanost.exe")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-password", "/password", "-pwd", "/pwd", "-startdate", "-enddate", "/startdate", "/enddate", "-from", "-to", "-range", "/range", "-since")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFileSHA256
title: PST Export by Non-Outlook Binary with Password and Date-Range Flags
id: 7e9a8b2c-3d4f-4a5b-9c1d-2e3f4a5b6c7d
description: Detects creation/modification of .pst files by a process other than Outlook/scanpst when the launching command line carries password or date-range flags - matches the bi-weekly mailbox-slice pattern from the stock exchange espionage campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hackers-spied-on-stock-exchange.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.collection
  - attack.t1114.001
  - attack.t1560.001
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_pst:
    TargetFilename|endswith: '.pst'
  selection_cli:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-password'
      - '/password'
      - '-startdate'
      - '-enddate'
      - '/startdate'
      - '/enddate'
      - '-range'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\scanpst.exe'
      - '\scanost.exe'
  condition: selection_pst and selection_cli and not filter_legit
falsepositives:
  - Sanctioned mailbox migration tooling (e.g. third-party PST exporters used during M&A)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:11 @TargetFilename:*.pst) AND (@CommandLine:(*-password* OR *\/password* OR *-startdate* OR *-enddate* OR *\/startdate* OR *\/enddate*))) -@Image:(*\\outlook.exe OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\\scanpst.exe OR *\\scanost.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\.pst$/i
| join({#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/(-|\/)(password|pwd|startdate|enddate|range|since)/i NOT ImageFileName=/\\(outlook|scanpst|scanost)\.exe$/i}, field=ContextProcessId, key=TargetProcessId, include=[ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="*.pst" Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=inner process_guid [| tstats `summariesonly` values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_name) as proc_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name!=outlook.exe Processes.process_name!=scanpst.exe (Processes.process="*password*" OR Processes.process="*startdate*" OR Processes.process="*enddate*" OR Processes.process="*-range*") by Processes.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_name="*.pst" Filesystem.action IN ("created","modified") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | join type=inner process_guid [| tstats summariesonly=false values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_name) as proc_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name!=outlook.exe Processes.process_name!=scanpst.exe (Processes.process="*password*" OR Processes.process="*startdate*" OR Processes.process="*enddate*" OR Processes.process="*-range*") by Processes.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`] | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] Scheduled task masquerading as Adobe/Lenovo/OneDrive system service Installation Medium
Hunts for schtasks.exe /create operations naming the task after Adobe, Lenovo or OneDrive when the parent process is not the corresponding genuine installer/updater. The Symantec write-up explicitly calls out scheduled tasks 'posing as Adobe, Lenovo and OneDrive system services' as the persistence layer. Rationale: The article explicitly names Adobe, Lenovo and OneDrive as the three vendors the attacker impersonated in scheduled-task names. Combining the schtasks /create command with those exact brand strings and a non-vendor parent process produces an article-specific pivot rather than a generic schtasks rule. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1036/005/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create", "-create")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Adobe", "Lenovo", "OneDrive")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("setup.exe", "msiexec.exe", "AdobeARM.exe", "Adobe_Updater.exe", "AdobeUpdateService.exe", "OneDriveSetup.exe", "OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe", "LenovoUpdate.exe", "SystemUpdate.exe", "trustedinstaller.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Adobe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files (x86)\Adobe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Microsoft OneDrive" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Lenovo"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\schtasks.exe"
| where CommandLine has_any ("/create", "-create")
| where CommandLine has_any ("Adobe", "Lenovo", "OneDrive")
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\setup.exe"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\msiexec.exe"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\AdobeARM.exe"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\OneDriveSetup.exe"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\LenovoUpdate.exe"
| where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\trustedinstaller.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName
title: Scheduled Task Masquerading as Adobe/Lenovo/OneDrive Service
id: 8a1b2c3d-4e5f-4a6b-9c1d-3e4f5a6b7c8d
description: Detects schtasks.exe /create commands whose task name impersonates Adobe, Lenovo, or OneDrive system services when the parent is not the corresponding vendor installer - matches the persistence masquerade in the Symantec stock-exchange espionage report.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hackers-spied-on-stock-exchange.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/04
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.t1053.005
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/create'
      - '-create'
  selection_name:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Adobe'
      - 'Lenovo'
      - 'OneDrive'
  filter_legit_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\setup.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
      - '\AdobeARM.exe'
      - '\OneDriveSetup.exe'
      - '\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe'
      - '\LenovoUpdate.exe'
      - '\trustedinstaller.exe'
  condition: selection_proc and selection_name and not filter_legit_parent
falsepositives:
  - In-house IT scripts re-creating Adobe/OneDrive update tasks via PowerShell
level: medium
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE) @CommandLine:(*\/create* OR *-create*) @CommandLine:(*Adobe* OR *Lenovo* OR *OneDrive*) -@ParentImage:(*\\AdobeARM.exe OR *\\OneDriveSetup.exe OR *\\OneDriveStandaloneUpdater.exe OR *\\LenovoUpdate.exe OR *\\trustedinstaller.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(\/|-)create/i
| CommandLine=/(Adobe|Lenovo|OneDrive)/i
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(setup|msiexec|AdobeARM|Adobe_Updater|OneDriveSetup|OneDriveStandaloneUpdater|LenovoUpdate|trustedinstaller)\.exe$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe (Processes.process="*/create*" OR Processes.process="*-create*") (Processes.process="*Adobe*" OR Processes.process="*Lenovo*" OR Processes.process="*OneDrive*") Processes.parent_process_name!=setup.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=msiexec.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=AdobeARM.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=OneDriveSetup.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=LenovoUpdate.exe by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name=schtasks.exe (Processes.process="*/create*" OR Processes.process="*-create*") (Processes.process="*Adobe*" OR Processes.process="*Lenovo*" OR Processes.process="*OneDrive*") Processes.parent_process_name!=setup.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=msiexec.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=AdobeARM.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=OneDriveSetup.exe Processes.parent_process_name!=LenovoUpdate.exe by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`
[LLM] FRPC (Fast Reverse Proxy client) execution by config-file argument Command & Control Medium
Hunts for execution of frpc.exe or any renamed binary running with the distinctive FRPC config-file argument pattern. Symantec's published indicator set explicitly lists FRPC as the tunneling tool used in the intrusion kit alongside the mailbox stealer. Rationale: FRPC is named outright in the Symantec indicator bundle. Its config file is canonically frpc.ini (or .toml in newer builds) — covering both the binary name and the config-arg pattern catches renamed-binary variants used to evade naive name-only rules. Cross-checked against the public fatedier/frp GitHub repo for argument conventions. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/fatedier/frp • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1572/
ATT&CKT1572 T1090
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "frpc.exe"
    or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("frpc.ini", "frpc.toml", "frpc.yaml")
    or ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s+-c\s+\S*frpc\.(ini|toml|yaml)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, SHA256, MD5
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\frpc.exe"
    or CommandLine has_any ("frpc.ini", "frpc.toml", "frpc.yaml")
    or CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)\s+-c\s+\S*frpc\.(ini|toml|yaml)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
title: FRPC Fast Reverse Proxy Client Execution
id: 9b2c3d4e-5f6a-4b7c-9d2e-4f5a6b7c8d9e

[LLM] curl/non-browser binary uploading to Dropbox or OneDrive personal API endpoints Actions on Objectives High
Detects curl, wget or other non-browser executables making outbound connections to Dropbox API hosts or OneDrive personal endpoints. Matches the article's exfiltration mechanic — the attacker pulled a Dropbox API token, uploaded with curl, and used OneDrive Personal to blend into normal cloud traffic. Rationale: The article explicitly names curl + Dropbox API tokens for the exfil channel and OneDrive Personal as the alternative. Pairing those destinations with non-browser process initiators (which never legitimately need to hit personal-cloud APIs on a corporate executive's workstation) yields a tight, article-specific detection. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1567/002/ • https://www.dropbox.com/developers/documentation/http/documentation
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Endpoint.Processes
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe", "wget.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe", "rclone.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("api.dropboxapi.com", "content.dropboxapi.com", "files.dropbox.com", "dropboxusercontent.com", "onedrive.live.com", "storage.live.com", "my.microsoftpersonalcontent.com")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("api.dropboxapi.com", "content.dropboxapi.com", "Authorization: Bearer", "Dropbox-API-Arg")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where SrcUsername != ""
| where DstHostname has_any ("api.dropboxapi.com", "content.dropboxapi.com", "files.dropbox.com", "dropboxusercontent.com", "onedrive.live.com", "storage.live.com")
| join kind=inner (
    ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where ActingProcessName in~ ("curl.exe", "wget.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "certutil.exe", "bitsadmin.exe", "rclone.exe")
        or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("api.dropboxapi.com", "content.dropboxapi.com", "Dropbox-API-Arg")
) on $left.DvcHostname == $right.DvcHostname
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
title: Non-Browser Binary Connecting to Dropbox or OneDrive Personal API

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/

    - attack.t1204.002

    product: windows

    selection_parent:

            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'

            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["ef641e956f91d501b748085996303c96a64d67f63bfeef0dda175e5aa19cca90", "5926b86b642e00672252953eb30d8f75cfb7797fe3118bd6fa2cfbee92905d61", "ceff7c51d70832c3ec8dd2744b606a23b3c924ef664ae23439b9b742ea154108", "da39146ef451d1b174a24d00b1e2a45cd38d54e849737f8f35333dcb22175707", "e3dbe63aded45278f49c4746ab938ed9472b36def79b43e2dd2d7eff014481d1", "82d83274680df928fdda296a348e01802f595e412308c399565c320df444052a", "288f26c2eadcb1a7923fe376d16f5404216cce15d9fc162a4a78574dc7df399a", "8bf051251ec3b973e39a313547e53421a2f8d2f6", "608d01124cd6b5b8c55888e984b4c4d9b06fa686", "ab9903d9edc720d1e11ea7d3d3e7a1c456f44ff7"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TA4922 phishing lure themes (payroll/VAT/tax/HR) into EU recipients Delivery Medium
Hunts inbound emails using TA4922's localized phishing lures (payroll, tax-audit, VAT filing, government, invoice, HR) into Germany/Italy/UK/South Africa recipients, especially those containing URLs to the campaign's C2 domains. Article-specific because it pivots on the four-country target set + the named C2 hostnames. Rationale: Pivots on the four lure themes the article explicitly lists (payroll/VAT/tax/invoice/HR) localized to the named target countries (German + Italian translations included), correlated with the three pre-extracted C2 domains. Sentinel query uses OfficeActivity (no DeviceName column) since this is mailflow telemetry.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1566.002 T1566.003
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email
let LureRegex = @"(?i)(payroll|lohnabrechnung|gehaltsabrechnung|vat|umsatzsteuer|iva|tax\s*audit|steuerpr(ü|ue)fung|verifica\s*fiscale|invoice|rechnung|fattura|hr\s*notice|personalabteilung|compliance\s*notice|vat\s*filing)";
let C2Domains = dynamic(["aeya388.club","ws.ztts88.cyou","nwphotoblog.com"]);
let UrlMatches = EmailUrlInfo
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where UrlDomain has_any (C2Domains)
| project NetworkMessageId, MatchedUrl = Url, MatchedDomain = UrlDomain;
EmailEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where EmailDirection =~ "Inbound"
| where DeliveryAction in~ ("Delivered","DeliveredAsSpam")
| where Subject matches regex LureRegex
     or NetworkMessageId in ((UrlMatches | project NetworkMessageId))
| join kind=leftouter UrlMatches on NetworkMessageId
| project Timestamp, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress, Subject, EmailLanguage, SenderIPv4, MatchedUrl, MatchedDomain, NetworkMessageId
| order by Timestamp desc
let LureRegex = @"(?i)(payroll|lohnabrechnung|gehaltsabrechnung|vat|umsatzsteuer|iva|tax\s*audit|steuerpr(ü|ue)fung|verifica\s*fiscale|invoice|rechnung|fattura|hr\s*notice|personalabteilung|compliance\s*notice)";
let C2Domains = dynamic(["aeya388.club","ws.ztts88.cyou","nwphotoblog.com"]);
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where OfficeWorkload =~ "Exchange"
| where (Subject matches regex LureRegex)
     or (Parameters has_any (C2Domains))
     or (EventData has_any (C2Domains))
| project TimeGenerated, Operation, UserId, ClientIP, Subject, Recipients, Sender = P2Sender, MessageId = InternetMessageId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TA4922 C2 callback to Atlas RAT / RomulusLoader infrastructure Command & Control High
Detects endpoint network egress to any of the five TA4922 C2 IPs or three C2 domains identified by Proofpoint, with the initiating process surfaced so analysts can pivot to the loader / RAT binary. Article-specific because it bolts directly to the pre-extracted IOC bundle. Rationale: Uses the five C2 IPs and three C2 domains pre-extracted from the Proofpoint IOC bundle. High-confidence atomic indicator match. Sentinel query uses CommonSecurityLog/DnsEvents/ImNetworkSession with their correct host-identifier columns (SourceHostName / Computer / DvcHostname) — no DeviceName references.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS

let C2Domains = dynamic(["aeya388.club","ws.ztts88.cyou","nwphotoblog.com"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2IPs)
     or RemoteUrl has_any (C2Domains)

[LLM] Atlas RAT anti-sandbox probes for Application Guard / CExecSvc / OS UUID Exploitation Medium
Catches Atlas RAT's pre-execution environment fingerprint: registry reads of Microsoft Defender Application Guard keys, queries for the CExecSvc service, and reads of SMBIOS / OS UUID — all from a single short-lived process burst. Article-specific: Proofpoint explicitly enumerates these three checks. Rationale: Pivots on the three specific environment checks Proofpoint named (Application Guard registry keys, CExecSvc service, OS UUID via WMIC csproduct). The triple-probe pattern from one process is high-fidelity because legitimate sandbox-detection tooling is rare on user endpoints.
ATT&CKT1497.001 T1082 T1012
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Registry
let AppGuardKeys = dynamic([@"HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Hvsi", @"HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\HVSI", @"SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CExecSvc"]);
let RegProbes = DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryKeyOpened","RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has_any (AppGuardKeys) or RegistryKey has "CExecSvc"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName;
let UuidProbes = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("csproduct","uuid"))
     or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Win32_ComputerSystemProduct","UUID"))
     or (FileName =~ "reg.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Hvsi","CExecSvc","Application Guard"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, UuidProcessId = ProcessId, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256;
RegProbes
| join kind=inner UuidProbes on DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, Timestamp1)) <= 60
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RegistryKey, UuidCmdLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine1
| order by Timestamp desc
let AppGuardKeys = dynamic([@"HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Hvsi", @"HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\HVSI", @"SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CExecSvc"]);
let RegProbes = ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has_any (AppGuardKeys) or RegistryKey has "CExecSvc"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey;
let UuidProbes = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where (NewProcessName endswith "\\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("csproduct","uuid"))
     or (NewProcessName has_any ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and CommandLine has_any ("Win32_ComputerSystemProduct","UUID"))
     or (NewProcessName endswith "\\reg.exe" and CommandLine has_any ("Hvsi","CExecSvc","Application Guard"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, ProbeProcessName = NewProcessName, ProbeCmd = CommandLine, ParentProcessName;
RegProbes
| join kind=inner (UuidProbes) on $left.DvcHostname == $right.Computer
| where abs(datetime_diff('second', TimeGenerated, TimeGenerated1)) <= 60
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, RegistryKey, ProbeProcessName, ProbeCmd
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon ((@EventID:13 AND (@TargetObject:(*\Hvsi* OR *\HVSI* OR *\hvsi* OR *CExecSvc* OR *cexecsvc* OR *"Application Guard"*))) OR (@EventID:1 AND @CommandLine:(*csproduct* OR *Win32_ComputerSystemProduct* OR *"uuid"* OR *Hvsi* OR *CExecSvc*)))
(#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate OR #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2)
| (RegObjectName=/(Hvsi|CExecSvc|Application Guard)/i OR CommandLine=/(csproduct|Win32_ComputerSystemProduct|Hvsi|CExecSvc|Application Guard|\buuid\b)/i)
| ImageFileName=/(wmic|reg|powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i OR ContextImageFileName=/(wmic|reg|powershell|pwsh|cmd)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, ParentBaseFileName], function=[count(), collect([CommandLine, RegObjectName])])
| _count > 1

[LLM] SilentRunLoader Python-based Chrome credential / cookie theft Actions on Objectives High
Detects non-Chrome processes (especially python.exe, py.exe, pythonw.exe, or unsigned LOLBins) opening Chrome's Login Data, Cookies, Web Data, or Local State files — the exact targeting Proofpoint attributes to SilentRunLoader. Pivots on the Python-loader fingerprint rather than a generic credential-dumper template. Rationale: Pivots on the exact targeting Proofpoint named (Chrome credentials, cookies, browsing data) plus SilentRunLoader's Python runtime fingerprint. Chrome's User Data files are read only by Chrome / Google Updater in normal operation, so python.exe touching them is a high-confidence stealer signal.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1059.006
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed","FileOpened")
| where FolderPath has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\"
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Login Data-journal","Cookies","Cookies-journal","Web Data","Local State","Network\\Cookies")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe","pythonw.exe","py.exe","python3.exe","python3.11.exe","python3.12.exe")
     or (InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","GoogleUpdateComRegisterShell64.exe","explorer.exe","backupd.exe")
         and InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Google")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, FileName, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFilePath has @"\Google\Chrome\User Data\"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Login Data-journal","Cookies","Cookies-journal","Web Data","Local State")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python.exe","pythonw.exe","py.exe","python3.exe")
     or (ActingProcessName !has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","brave.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","explorer.exe"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: SilentRunLoader Chrome Credential Store Access by Python

[LLM] RomulusLoader-style unauthorized AnyDesk / SyncFuture install on EU endpoint Installation High
Detects fresh installs or first-time launches of AnyDesk and SyncFuture binaries — the RMM combo TA4922 weaponizes via RomulusLoader — on hosts that have never run them before. Pivots on SyncFuture (highly unusual outside Chinese deployments) and on AnyDesk launched by a non-installer parent. Rationale: SyncFuture is explicitly called out as a China-popular RMM that Proofpoint found on German victim hosts — its mere presence outside APAC is anomalous. AnyDesk on a first-seen-per-host basis catches the RomulusLoader handoff without alerting on routine vendor RMM use.
ATT&CKT1219 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
let Baseline = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp between (ago(90d) .. ago(14d))
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","SyncFuture.exe","SyncFutureSetup.exe")
| summarize by DeviceName, FileName;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","SyncFuture.exe","SyncFutureSetup.exe")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on DeviceName, FileName
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msiexec.exe","explorer.exe","AnyDesk.exe")
     or FileName in~ ("SyncFuture.exe","SyncFutureSetup.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let Baseline = SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated between (ago(90d) .. ago(14d))
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\AnyDesk.exe","\\SyncFuture.exe","\\SyncFutureSetup.exe")
| summarize by Computer, NewProcessName;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\AnyDesk.exe","\\SyncFuture.exe","\\SyncFutureSetup.exe")
| join kind=leftanti Baseline on Computer, NewProcessName
| where ParentProcessName !has_any ("\\msiexec.exe","\\explorer.exe","\\AnyDesk.exe")
     or NewProcessName has_any ("\\SyncFuture.exe","\\SyncFutureSetup.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

[LLM] TA4922 loader / Atlas RAT known SHA256 file write or execution Installation High
Atomic-indicator detection on the eight SHA256s Proofpoint attributes to RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, Atlas RAT, and the Winos4.0/ValleyRAT samples. Useful as a tripwire even after C2 takedown. Rationale: Eight pre-extracted SHA256s from the Proofpoint IOC bundle, covering RomulusLoader, SilentRunLoader, Atlas RAT, and ValleyRAT/Winos4.0 samples. Atomic match — low FP unless analysts deliberately detonate.

[LLM] Atlas RAT operator-driven host shutdown / reboot impact Actions on Objectives Medium
Catches the article's stated Atlas RAT impact capability: operator-triggered system shutdown/reboot. Correlates Windows shutdown/reboot events with a recent C2 connection from the same host so legitimate WSUS / GPO reboots don't drown the signal. Rationale: Article explicitly lists 'System shutdown/reboot commands' as an Atlas RAT capability. The C2-correlation join (shutdown within 4h of a beacon to the listed IOC IPs/domains) is what differentiates this from WSUS/GPO-driven reboots, which dominate raw 1074/6006/6008 volume.
ATT&CKT1529

C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession

| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId
